14nov1549.summary: Charles V tells his governor of Milan not to make terms with Ottavio Farnese over Parma: Ottavio has no money or troops, and it would mean war with the Church, which holds Parma, and could drive the Pope to give it to Orazio Farnese. Gonzaga may act only in two cases, an Orsini stroke or Orazio's entry, and then with dissimulation.
14nov1549.en:
c.60r, first block. And coming to the particular matter of the decision with which you stood [..] to arrange and make terms with Duke Ottavio over the enterprise of Parma, some of the considerations that occur to us about it will be touched on here, so as afterwards [..] to make known to you our intention and will.

c.60r, second block. Having regard to how little foundation can be placed in the person of the said Duke Ottavio for an enterprise such as that of Parma, both for what is known of it and for his having no means of getting money, being in disgrace with the Pollo; and because even if he did not lack it, he has nowhere to draw the troops from, there being no neighbouring lands there from which he could get them except those of the Church of et ud and tu;

20nov1549.summary: After Paul III's death: five short cipher passages forbid any move on Parma during the vacancy of the see, or any war on the Church, and put off an attack on the Farnese. The clerk's margin notes give the same sense.
20nov1549.en:
Clear: as to what you ask, in case the College should wish to confirm and defend [2 lines of signs not read]:
1. in Parma in the name of the Church. Clear: given what is said above of our intention.
2. Clear: in no way let [anything] be moved in Parma on our part, nor in any other place.
3. Clear: claim that we wished to move war against the Church, directly or indirectly.
4. Clear: have, to offend and occupy on this occasion the state of the house of Farnese, because of the neighbourhood it has with that of the said [Duke of Florence].
5. Clear: nor should it be attempted at such a time, since when, after the pontiff has been elected, something else should seem right and give occasion, it can easily be done.

30sep1549.summary: Someone is dealing with the Prior of Lombardy, castellan of the castle of Nice, so as to throw him out and put in Brissac. The clear margin note says the same in brief and was in view.
30sep1549.en: And although he went with the aim of dealing with the Prior of Lombardy, who is castellan of the castle, in such a way that it would amount to throwing him out of there in order to put in Mons. de Brissac.

13may1549.summary: Gonzaga is to work out where the money and materials for a work will come from, without letting the intention show. The slip c.29 is the contemporary decipherment.
13may1549.en: And consider in the meantime where and how the money for the work and also the materials is to be had, so as to save time, without any show being made by which it could be understood or imagined that this is our intention.

23dec1549.summary: On Nice and the Prior of Lombardy, who is sent money and told to go and live in the castle. c.77 is the contemporary decipherment.
23dec1549.en: a. as to Parma. b. Duke Ottavio. c. about Nice, that place being of the importance it is and the Prior of Lombardy being away from it. d. to the said Prior on account of the said pay, charging him to go at once to attend and reside in the castle.

system: Imperial Cipher of 1544-1554: a syllabary in which the base shape gives the consonant and a mark the vowel (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, o-loop o, p-tail u), with alphabet signs, double-letter signs and nulls. Clear words stand in the cipher as code words.
